title: Fused Signal Autoscaler: latency + cost targets with safety horizon
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an autoscaling policy engine that fuses latency and cost signals to meet tenant-level throughput guarantees while enforcing strict safety limits. The goal is a multi-objective controller that prefers latency SLOs up to a cost budget, with graceful degradation and constrained surge behavior for Dedicated GPU pools. Deliverables: policy spec, simulator harness, runtime implementation plan, and rollout safety checks.
updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff — scoped to Dedicated tier only. Identified primary signals: p50/p95 latency, request throughput, per-tenant tokens/sec, and estimated GPU token cost. Decided to pursue a fused-signal approach rather than separate controllers to avoid oscillations when signals cross (e.g., reduced batch size lowers latency but raises cost).

2026-02-25: Algorithm selection — prototyped two candidate controllers in sim: (A) priority-weighted PI controller that blends latency error and cost pressure, (B) event-based reservoir scaler with admission budget. PI variant is simpler; reservoir has stronger safety envelope during sudden bursts. Team vote 6-3 in favor of reservoir as default with PI as opt-in for low-latency tenants.

2026-02-28: Safety limits defined — max_step_up = 30% of pool capacity per minute, max_step_down = 50% per minute, cool_down_window = 90s between successive scale-ups, surge_budget_per_tenant = 20% reserved headroom, global_eviction_policy = rate-first eviction of bursty best-effort tenants. Added metric floor checks to prevent oscillation on noisy p50 signals.

2026-03-02: Simulation results — ran workload mix: steady baseline + 10% random microbursts + 2 synthetic tenant spikes. Reservoir scaler met p95 SLO in 94% of runs and kept cost delta <12% vs baseline. PI controller achieved slightly better median latency but had 25% more oscillation during repeated spikes.

2026-03-03: Implementation plan — split work across runtime team and orchestrator: (1) policy compiler to translate high-level SLOs into ramp schedules and reservoir quotas; (2) runtime admission hooks to enforce per-request token budgeting and prefetch hints; (3) telemetry additions: per-tenant surge_utilization, reservoir_level, last_scale_event. Runtime changes estimated 5 sprint points.

2026-03-04: Security/operational review notes — ops requested a forced-fallback flag that pins pools to a safe minimum during incidents, and a read-only mode to surface current reservoir state in Console. Added to spec and marked as release blocker until Console exposure is validated.
comments: PM (Jordan Li): Please ensure the policy surfaced in Console explains cost trade-offs to customers and includes recommended tenant defaults. Add a migration path for existing Dedicated customers with custom autoscale settings.
Design (Rae Kim): Need UX mockups for 'surge budget' visibility and for manually overriding the reservoir in emergencies. Will attach mocks next week (Confluence link placeholder).

Reviewer (SRE - Elena Torres): Concern about eviction strategy causing churn on multi-tenant pools. Suggest adding a cooldown after eviction before re-admitting evicted tenants. Also ask for an incident runbook section.
Engineering (Marcus Chen): Implementing reservoir persistence across controller restarts to avoid sudden drops. Plan: write small checkpoint to control-plane KV and reconcile on startup.
notes_and_links: Rollout plan snippet: gradual -> 10% pools -> 30% -> 100% with canary detection on p95 and reservoir depletion
